3dee797156:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>N</c>octe surgéntes vigilémus omnes,
Semper in psalmis meditémur, atque
Víribus totis Dómino canámus
Dúlciter hymnos.

<h>U</h>t pio Regi páriter canéntes,
Cum suis Sanctis mereámur aulam
Íngredi cæli, simul et beátam
Dúcere vitam.

<h>P</h>ræstet hoc nobis Déitas beáta
Patris, ac Nati, paritérque Sancti
Spíritus, cujus réboat per omnem
Glória mundum.
Amen.
7798d5e712:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow, from the slumbers of the night arising,
Chant we the holy psalmody of David,
Hymns to our Master, with a voice concordant,
Sweetly intoning.

<h>S</h>o may our Monarch pitifully hear us,
That we may merit with his saints to enter
Mansions eternal, therewithal possessing
Joy beatific.

<h>T</h>his be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the mercy of Christ bring us to the joys of paradise.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Ad Timotheum 2 2:22-26</r>
But flee thou youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, charity, and peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. And avoid foolish and unlearned questions, knowing that they beget strifes. But the servant of the Lord must not wrangle: but be mild towards all men, apt to teach, patient, With modesty admonishing them that resist the truth: if peradventure God may give them repentance to know the truth, And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Te Deum</h>
<r>Canticum SS. Ambrosii et Augustini</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * majestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ majestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Judex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
6dd1763062:
<h>Te Deum</h>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

<r>2 Thess 3</r>
<c>D</c>óminus dírigat corda et córpora nostra in caritáte Dei, et patiéntia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ucis Creátor óptime,
Lucem diérum próferens,
Primórdiis lucis novæ,
Mundi parans oríginem:

<h>Q</h>ui mane iunctum vésperi
Diem vocári prǽcipis:
Tetrum chaos illábitur,
Audi preces cum flétibus.

<h>N</h>e mens graváta crímine,
Vitæ sit exsul múnere,
Dum nil perénne cógitat,
Seséque culpis ílligat.

<h>C</h>ælórum pulset íntimum,
Vitále tollat prǽmium:
Vitémus omne nóxium:
Purgémus omne péssimum.

<h>P</h>ræsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

9e36b8df3d:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>2 Thess 3</r>
<c>A</c>nd the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> blest Creator of the light,
Who mak’st the day with radiance bright,
And o’er the forming world didst call
The light from chaos first of all;

<h>W</h>hose wisdom joined in meet array
The morn and eve, and named them day:
Night comes with all its darkling fears;
Regard thy people’s prayers and tears.

<h>L</h>est, sunk in sin, and whelmed with strife,
They lose the gift of endless life;
While thinking but the thoughts of time,
They weave new chains of woe and crime.

<h>B</h>ut grant them grace that they may strain
The heavenly gate and prize to gain:
Each harmful lure aside to cast,
And purge away each error past.

<h>O</h> Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, direct my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> As incense in thy sight.

aff2c80ed5:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>T</c>e lucis ante términum,
Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
Ut sólita cleméntia
Sis præsul ad custódiam.

<h>P</h>rocul recédant sómnia,
Et nóctium phantásmata;
Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
Ne polluántur córpora.

<h>P</h>ræsta, Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
08fbe66a8b:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>B</c>efore the ending of the day,
Creator of the world, we pray
That with thy wonted favor thou
Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

<h>F</h>rom all ill dreams defend our eyes,
From nightly fears and fantasies;
Tread under foot our ghostly foe,
That no pollution we may know.

<h>O</h> Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Keep us, O Lord, as the apple of thine eye.
<r>℟.</r> Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

407c332e98:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>V</c>ísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: et Ángeli tui sancti habitántes in ea nos in pace custódiant, et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
Per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus: per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
f5b5bd304d:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>V</c>isit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
18164f80d9:

<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
<r>Benedictio.</r> <n>Given by the Prior, without chant (not on Maundy Thursday and Good Friday):</n> Benedíctio Dei omnipoténtis Patris, et Fílii, ✠ et Spíritus Sancti descéndat super vos, et máneat semper.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>In the absence of the Prior, the Subprior or the Hebdomadarian gives it, saying not super vos but super nos.</n>
ae06173a7e:
<h>Conclusion</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<r>℣.</r> Let us bless the Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the blessing of almighty God, the Father, the Son, ✠ and the Holy Ghost, come down upon you and remain for ever.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
d0d30257cc:
<h>Ad processionem in fine Completorii</h>
<n>After the blessing the Salve Regina is begun by two cantors (on Doubles and Totum Duplex) or by one; at its beginning all prostrate, or kneel in Paschaltide, until "Salve Regina" has been sung; then the procession goes into the church and the Hebdomadarian sprinkles the brethren with holy water.</n>
<r>Ant.</r> Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ: Vita, dulcédo et spes nostra, salve. Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ. Ad te suspirámus, geméntes et flentes in hac lacrimárum valle. Eia ergo, advocáta nostra, illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte. Et Jesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui, nobis post hoc exsílium osténde. O clemens, O pia, O dulcis Virgo María.
<r>℣.</r> Dignáre me laudáre te, Virgo sacráta.
<r>℟.</r> Da mihi virtútem contra hostes tuos.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>C</c>oncéde nos fámulos tuos, quǽsumus, Dómine Deus, perpétua mentis et córporis salúte gaudére: et gloriósa beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis intercessióne a præsénti liberári tristítia, et ætérna pérfrui lætítia: Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> O lumen Ecclésiæ, Doctor veritátis, Rosa patiéntiæ, Ebur castitátis, Aquam sapiéntiæ propinásti gratis: Prædicátor grátiæ, nos junge beátis.
<r>℣.</r> Ora pro nobis, beáte Pater Domínice.
<r>℟.</r> Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>C</c>oncéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui peccatórum nostrórum póndere prémimur, beáti Domínici Confessóris tui, Patris nostri, patrocínio sublevémur: Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Then Pater noster and Credo in Deum, said silently.</n>
66f77f2a16:
<h>Procession at the end of Compline</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.
<r>℣.</r> Make me worthy to praise thee, holy Virgin.
<r>℟.</r> Give me strength against thine enemies.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, O Lord God, that we thy servants may enjoy perpetual health of mind and body; and by the glorious intercession of blessed Mary ever Virgin, be delivered from present sorrow and enjoy eternal gladness. Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> O light of the Church, teacher of truth, rose of patience, ivory of chastity, freely thou didst pour forth the waters of wisdom: preacher of grace, unite us with the blessed.
<r>℣.</r> Pray for us, blessed Father Dominic.
<r>℟.</r> That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who are weighed down by the burden of our sins may be raised up by the patronage of blessed Dominic, thy Confessor, our Father. Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>L</h>inguam refrénans témperet,

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow in the sun's new dawning ray,
Lowly of heart, our God we pray
That he from harm may keep us free
In all the deeds this day shall see.

<h>M</h>ay fear of him our tongues restrain,
Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:
His favouring care our guardian be,
Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

<h>M</h>ay every heart be pure from sin
And folly find no place therein:
Scant need of food, excess denied,
Wear down in us the body's pride.

<h>T</h>hat when the light of day is gone,
And night in course shall follow on.
We, free from cares the world affords,
May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be,
All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

Who orderest time and change aright,
Who send’st the early morning ray,
And light’st the glow of perfect day:

<h>E</h>xtinguish thou each sinful fire,
And banish every ill desire;
And while thou keep’st the body whole,
Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

<h>A</h>lmighty Father, hear our cry,
Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> strength and stay upholding all creation,
Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,
Yet day by day the light in due gradation
From hour to hour through all its changes guide:

<h>G</h>rant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,
An eve untouched by shadows of decay,
The brightness of a holy death-bed blending
With dawning glories of th’ eternal day.

<h>H</h>ear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,
And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,
Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living
Now and to endless ages art adored.
Amen.

998e84c026:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Eccli. 45</r>
<c>D</c>iléctus Deo, et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est: símilem illum fecit in glória sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Sancte Simon Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos: * Et impetrátam cǽlitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.
<r>℣.</r> O sancte Simon, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia. Et impetrátam.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Tu defer.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum.
<r>℟.</r> Stolam glóriæ índuit eum.
889bdcf498:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Eccli. 45</r>
<c>D</c>iléctus Deo, et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est: símilem illum fecit in glória sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Sancte Simon Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos: * Et impetrátam cǽlitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.
<r>℣.</r> O sancte Simon, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord loved him and beautified him.
<r>℟.</r> He clothed him with a robe of glory.

<r>℣.</r> Præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo * Salutári nostro.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo * Salutári nostro.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.

<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.

<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.

<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.

c61fbeb46f:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.
f6707b2954:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. He that could have transgressed, and hath not transgressed: and could do evil things, and hath not done them: Therefore are his goods established in the Lord, and all the church of the saints shall declare his alms.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Eccli. 45</r>
<c>D</c>iléctus Deo, et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est: símilem illum fecit in glória sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Sancte Cárole Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos: * Et impetrátam cǽlitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.
<r>℣.</r> O sancte Cárole, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia. Et impetrátam.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Tu defer.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum.
<r>℟.</r> Stolam glóriæ índuit eum.
5b3e30c18d:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>

<r>℣.</r> O sancte Cárole, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord loved him and beautified him.
<r>℟.</r> He clothed him with a robe of glory.

<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.

<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> In manu tua, Dómine, * Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> In manu tua, Dómine, * Omnes fines terræ.

49cc23be7c:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Confessórum Regem adorémus, * Qui cæléstis regni méritum et glóriam cóntulit sancto suo Cárolo
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Qui cæléstis regni méritum et glóriam cóntulit sancto suo Cárolo
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Confessórum Regem adorémus, * Qui cæléstis regni méritum et glóriam cóntulit sancto suo Cárolo
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Qui cæléstis regni méritum et glóriam cóntulit sancto suo Cárolo
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Confessórum Regem adorémus, * Qui cæléstis regni méritum et glóriam cóntulit sancto suo Cárolo
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Qui cæléstis regni méritum et glóriam cóntulit sancto suo Cárolo

05adfc0704:
<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lectio (in præparatione).</n>
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Euge serve bone, et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam: * Intra in gáudium dómini tui.
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, quinque talénta tradidísti mihi, ecce ália quinque superlucrátus sum. Intra in gáudium.
4b44b23f76:
<h>Lesson 1</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the everlasting Father bless us with an everlasting blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Lesson (in preparation).</n>
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Well done, thou good and faithful servant, thou hast been faithful over a few things. I will make thee ruler over many things: * Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Lord, Thou deliverest unto me five talents behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.
600f1534f2:
<h>Lectio ii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adjuváre dignétur.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Ad Titum 1:4, 7-9</r>
<c>A</c> Portet epíscopum sine crímine esse, sicut Dei dispensatórem: non supérbum, non iracúndum, non vinoléntum, non percussórem, non turpis lucri cúpidum: sed hospitálem, benígnum, sóbrium, justum, sanctum, continéntem, amplecténtem eum, qui secúndum doctrínam est, fidélem sermónem: ut potens sit exhortári in doctrína sana, et eos, qui contradícunt, argúere.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium ii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Justus germinábit sicut lílium: * Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.
<r>℣.</r> Plantátus in domo Dómini, in átriis domus Dei nostri. Et florébit in.
143d20b106:
<h>Lesson 2</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the only-begotten Son of God vouchsafe to bless and help us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Ad Titum 1:4, 7-9</r>
To Titus my beloved son, according to the common faith, grace and peace from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus our Saviour. For a bishop must be without crime, as the steward of God: not proud, not subject to anger, not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre: But given to hospitality, gentle, sober, just, holy, continent: Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine, that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine, and to convince the gainsayers.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> The righteous shall grow as the lily * Yea, he shall flourish in the presence of the Lord for ever.
<r>℣.</r> Those that be planted in the house of the Lord, shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
b157596430:
<h>Lectio iv</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>A</c>d sancti ac beatíssimi Patris nostri Cároli, cujus hódie festa celebrámus, laudes addidísse áliquid, decerpsísse est; síquidem virtútem ejus grátia, non sermónibus exponénda est, sed opéribus comprobánda. Cum enim dicat Scriptúra: Glória patris est fílius sápiens; quantæ hujus sunt glóriæ, qui tantórum filiórum sapiéntia et devotióne lætátur? In Christo Confessóris Ponti enim Jesu per Evangélium ipse nos génuit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium iv</h>
<r>℟.</r> Magnificávit eum in conspéctu regum, * Et dedit illi corónam glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Státuit illi testaméntum sempitérnum, et beatificávit illum in glória. Et dedit illi.
51cd4ccb29:
<h>Lesson 4</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May God the Father almighty be gracious and merciful unto us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
From the Sermons of St Maximus, Bishop [of Turin.] It is idle to strive to add anything to the praise of our holy and most blessed Father Carolus whose Feast is this day kept. The beauty of his life ought not to be the subject of panegyrics, so much as the object of imitation. The Scripture saith “A wise son is the glory of his father,” truly then will he be honoured by such as, by doing after his en sample, show themselves to be his children for in Christ Jesus hath he begotten us through the Gospel.(1 Cor. iv. 15.)
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Magnificávit eum in conspéctu regum, * Et dedit illi corónam glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Státuit illi testaméntum sempitérnum, et beatificávit illum in glória.

<h>Responsorium vi</h>
<r>℟.</r> Sancte Cárole Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos, * Et impetrátam cǽlitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.
<r>℣.</r> O sancte Cárole, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia. Et impetrátam.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Tu defer indulgéntiam.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Eccli. 45</r>
<c>D</c>iléctus Deo, et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est: símilem illum fecit in glória sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Sancte Martíne Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos: * Et impetrátam cǽlitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.
<r>℣.</r> O sancte Martíne, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia. Et impetrátam.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Tu defer.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> O sancte Martíne, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia, servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Quóniam ipse fecit nos.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Hebr. 11</r>
<c>S</c>ancti per fidem vicérunt regna, operáti sunt justítiam, adépti sunt repromissiónes, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Lavérunt stolas suas, et cándidas eas fecérunt. * In sánguine Agni.
<r>℣.</r> Isti sunt, qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas. In sánguine Agni.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. In sánguine Agni.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>S</c>anctórum méritis ínclyta gáudia
Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
Nam gliscit ánimus prómere cántibus
Victórum genus óptimum.

<h>H</h>i sunt quos rétinens mundus inhórruit:
Ipsum nam stérili flore peráridum
Sprevére pénitus, teque secúti sunt,
Rex Christe bone cǽlitus.

<h>H</h>i pro te fúrias atque ferócia
Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
Cessit his lácerans fórtiter úngula,
Nec carpsit penetrália.

<h>C</h>ædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
Non murmur résonat, non querimónia:
Sed corde tácito mens bene cónscia
Consérvat patiéntiam.

<h>Q</h>uæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
Quæ tu Martyribus múnera prǽparas?
Rubri nam flúido sánguine láureis
Ditántur bene fúlgidis.

<h>T</h>e summa Déitas únaque póscimus,
Ut culpas ábluas, nóxia súbtrahas,
Des pacem fámulis, nos quoque glóriam
Per cuncta tibi sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Lætámini in Dómino, et exsultáte justi.
<r>℟.</r> Et gloriámini omnes recti corde.
cf49fe3bed:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Hebr. 11</r>
<c>S</c>ancti per fidem vicérunt regna, operáti sunt justítiam, adépti sunt repromissiónes, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Lavérunt stolas suas, et cándidas eas fecérunt. * In sánguine Agni.
<r>℣.</r> Isti sunt, qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>S</c>ing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!

<h>T</h>hey, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.

<h>L</h>ord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.

<h>W</h>hile they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.

<h>W</h>hat joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!

<h>Y</h>et we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.

<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte adorémus Regem regum, * Qui beátis Martýribus corónam dedit glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Qui beátis Martýribus corónam dedit glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte adorémus Regem regum, * Qui beátis Martýribus corónam dedit glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Qui beátis Martýribus corónam dedit glóriæ.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.

1ea9b1e5d3:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>S</c>anctórum méritis ínclyta gáudia
Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
Nam gliscit ánimus prómere cántibus
Victórum genus óptimum.

<h>H</h>i sunt quos rétinens mundus inhórruit:
Ipsum nam stérili flore peráridum
Sprevére pénitus, teque secúti sunt,
Rex Christe bone cǽlitus.

<h>H</h>i pro te fúrias atque ferócia
Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
Cessit his lácerans fórtiter úngula,
Nec carpsit penetrália.

<h>C</h>ædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
Non murmur résonat, non querimónia:
Sed corde tácito mens bene cónscia
Consérvat patiéntiam.

<h>Q</h>uæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
Quæ tu Martyribus múnera prǽparas?
Rubri nam flúido sánguine láureis
Ditántur bene fúlgidis.

<h>T</h>e summa Déitas únaque póscimus,
Ut culpas ábluas, nóxia súbtrahas,
Des pacem fámulis, nos quoque glóriam
Per cuncta tibi sǽcula.
Amen.
3b0bceaaac:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!

<h>T</h>hey, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.

<h>L</h>ord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.

<h>W</h>hile they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.

<h>W</h>hat joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!

<h>Y</h>et we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.

<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

<r>Rom 8:18-21</r>
<c>E</c>xístimo enim quod non sunt condígnæ passiónes hujus témporis ad futúram glóriam, quæ revelábitur in nobis. Nam exspectátio creatúræ revelatiónem filiórum Dei exspéctat. feda816703:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Jac. 1</r>
<c>B</c>eátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam, cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Gloriósus Dei amícus Petrus, Jesu Dómini confessióne fundátus, inter tormentórum supplícia stetit impertérritus: * Ac demum, triumpháli morte insígnis, Cælos petívit sánguine laureátus.
<r>℣.</r> Felíci commércio, pro terrénis cæléstia, pro peritúris ætérna commútans. Ac demum.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Cælos petívit.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>D</c>eus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.

<h>H</h>ic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blandiménta nóxia
Cadúca rite députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.

<h>P</h>œnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Pro te effúndens sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.

<h>O</h>b hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.

<h>L</h>aus et perénnis glória
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine.
<r>℟.</r> Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
5e4cd7b4b1:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jac. 1</r>
<c>B</c>lessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Gloriósus Dei amícus Petrus, Jesu Dómini confessióne fundátus, inter tormentórum supplícia stetit impertérritus: * Ac demum, triumpháli morte insígnis, Cælos petívit sánguine laureátus.
<r>℣.</r> Felíci commércio, pro terrénis cæléstia, pro peritúris ætérna commútans.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>G</h>lory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, O Lord.
<r>℟.</r> And madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

d43afe2c5e:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>2 Cor 1</r>
<c>B</c>enedíctus Deus et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>O</c> lux beáta Trínitas,
Et principális Únitas,
Jam sol recédit ígneus,
Infúnde lumen córdibus.

<h>T</h>e mane laudum cármine,
Te deprecémur véspere:
Te nostra supplex glória
Per cuncta laudet sǽcula.

<h>D</h>eo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.

<r>2 Cor 1</r>
<c>B</c>lessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> Trinity of blessed Light,
O Unity of sovereign might,
as now the fiery sun departs,
shed Thou Thy beams within our hearts.

<h>T</h>o Thee our morning song of praise,
to Thee our evening prayer we raise;
Thee may our glory evermore
in lowly reverence adore.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be;
all praise, Eternal Son, to Thee;
all glory, as is ever meet,
to God the Holy Paraclete.

<c>D</c>eus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.

<h>H</h>ic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blandiménta nóxia
Cadúca rite députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.

<h>P</h>œnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Pro te effúndens sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.

Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.

Deo Patri, et Fílio,

In sempitérna sǽcula.

532abfd581:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>G</h>lory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

What this second interpretation is the meaning of the Gospel, appeareth most probably from the words which follow And he that hateth his life in this world, shall keep it unto life eternal. From which we may suppose the sense of the first words to be He that loveth his life in this world shall lose it unto life eternal. This is a great and marvellous saying, showing how a man may so love life as to lose life, and so hate life as to keep life. If thou love it too well, then dost thou hate it if thou hate it with an holy hatred, then dost thou love it. Blessed are they that, lest they should so love it as to lose it, so hate it as to keep it.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.

<c>M</c>artyr of God, whose strength was steeled
To follow close God's only Son,
Well didst thou brave thy battlefield,
And well thy heavenly bliss was won!

<h>N</h>ow join thy prayers with ours, who pray
That God may pardon us and bless;
For prayer keeps evil's plague away,
And draws from life its weariness.

For us how many a bond remains!
O love of God release us all.

All praise to thee, Eternal Son;
All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,
While never-ending ages run.

<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew At that time, when Jesus was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him: And behold a leper came and adored him. And so on. Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.) When the Lord was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed Him. They were not able to follow Him when He went up. And first there came a leper. This poor creature's disease had prevented him from hearing the Saviour's long sermon on the Mount. Let it be noted that he is the first person specially named as being healed. The second was the Centurion's servant; the third was Peter's wife's mother, who was sick of a fever at Capernaum; the fourth were they who were brought unto Christ as being troubled with evil spirits, from whom He by His word cast out the evil spirits, at the same time that He healed all that were sick.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>e</c>t ecce leprósus véniens, adorábat eum, dicens. Recte post prædicatiónem atque doctrínam, signi offértur occásio, ut per virtútem miráculi, prætéritus apud audiéntes sermo firmétur. Dómine, si vis, potes me mundáre. Qui voluntátem rogat, de virtúte non dúbitat. Et exténdens Jesus manum tétigit eum, dicens: Volo, mundáre. Extendénte manum Dómino, statim lepra fugit. Simúlque consídera, quam húmilis, et sine jactántia respónsio. Dominica Ii. Post Lectio ix, Lue díxerat, Si vis: Dóminus respóndit, Volo. Ille præmíserat, Potes me mundáre: Dóminus jungit, et dicit, Mundáre. Non ergo, ut pleríque Latinórum putant, jungéndum est, et legéndum, Volo mundáre: sed separátim, ut primum dicat, Volo; deínde ímperet, Mundáre. Et ait illi Jesus: Vide, némini díxeris. Et revéra quid erat necésse ut sermóne jactáret, quod córpore præferébat? Sed vade, osténde te sacerdóti. Várias ob causas mittit eum ad sacerdótem: primum propter humilitátem, ut sacerdótibus deférre honórem videátur. Erat enim lege præcéptum, ut, qui mundáti fúerant a lepra, offérrent múnera sacerdótibus. Deínde, ut mundátum vidéntes leprósum, aut créderent Salvatóri, aut non créderent: st créderent, salvaréntur; si non créderent, inexcusábiles forent. Et simul, ne, quod in eo sæpíssime criminabántur, legem viderétur infríngere.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte adorémus.

Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,

At his petition.

Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,

<c>Q</c>uotiescúmque, fratres caríssimi, altáris vel templi festivitátem cólimus, si fidéliter ac diligénter atténdimus et sancte ac juste vívimus, quidquid in templis manufáctis ágitur, totum in nobis spiritáli ædificatióne complétur. Non enim mentítus est ille qui dixit: Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos; et Ix Anniversario quia córpora vestra templum sunt Spíritus vestra Sancti, qui in vobis est? Et ideo, fratres caríssimi, quia, nullis præcedéntibus méritis, sed per grátiam Dei merúimus fíeri templum Dei, quantum possumus cum ipsíus adjutório labóremus, ne Dóminus noster in templo suo, hoc est, in nobis ipsis, invéniat quod óculos suæ majestátis offéndat.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

2c16205853:
<h>Lesson 4</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May God the Father almighty be gracious and merciful unto us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo.) Dearly beloved brethren, as often as we keep the Dedication-Feast of some Altar or Church, if we think faithfully and carefully, and live holily and righteously, that which is done in temples made with hands, is done in our soul by a spiritual building. He at the Dedication of the Temple. lied not who said: The temple of God is holy; which temple ye are (i Cor. iii. 17,) and again: Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost, Which is in you, (vi. 19.) And therefore, dearly beloved brethren, since by the grace of God, without any foregoing deserts of our own, we have been made meet to become the Temple of God, let us work as hard as we can, with His help, that our Lord may not find in His Temple, that is, in us, anything to offend the eyes of His Majesty.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Tu defer.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.

<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

From the Sermons of St Maximus, Bishop [of Turin.] It is idle to strive to add anything to the praise of our holy and most blessed Father Albertus whose Feast is this day kept. The beauty of his life ought not to be the subject of panegyrics, so much as the object of imitation. The Scripture saith “A wise son is the glory of his father,” truly then will he be honoured by such as, by doing after his en sample, show themselves to be his children for in Christ Jesus hath he begotten us through the Gospel.(1 Cor. iv. 15.)
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.

<r>Benedictio.</r> Evangélica léctio sit nobis salus et protéctio.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Respóndens Jesus discípulis suis ait illis: Habéte fidem Dei. Amen dico vobis quia quicúmque díxerit huic monti: Tóllere et míttere in mare, et non hæsitáverit in corde suo, sed credíderit quia quodcúmque díxerit fiat, fiet el Et réliqua. Venerábilis Bedæ Presbýteri (Lib. Mare, cap. ll.) Olent Gentiles qui contra Ecclésiam maledicta scripsére, improperare nostris quod non habúerint plenam fidem Dei, quia numquam montes transferre potúerint. Quibus respondéndum est non scripta esse, quæ in Ecclésia sunt gesta, sicut étiam de factis ipsíus Christi et Dómini nostri Scriptúra testátur. Unde et hoc quoque fíeri potuísset, ut mons ablátus de terra mitterétur mare, si necessitas id fíeri poposcísset. Quómodo légimus factum precibus beáti Patris Gregórii, Neocæsaréæ Ponti antístitis, viri meritis et virtútibus exímii, ut mons in terra tantum loco cederet quantum íncolæ civitátis opus habebant.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium vii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Audívi vocem de cælo veniéntem: Veníte omnes vírgines sapientíssimæ, * Óleum recóndite in vasis vestris, dum sponsus advénerit.
<r>℣.</r> Média nocte clamor factus est: Ecce sponsus venit. Óleum recóndite in.
a86153133b:
<h>Lesson 7</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the Gospel reading be our salvation and protection.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
From the Holy Gospel according to Mark And Jesus answering, saith to them: Have the faith of God. Amen I say to you, that whosoever shall say to this mountain, Be thou removed and be cast into the sea, and shall not stagger in his heart, but believe, that whatsoever he saith shall be done; it shall be done unto him. And so on. Homily by the Venerable Bede, Priest (at Jarrow.) The heathen, who have written blasphemies against the Church, are used to cast in our teeth that we have not full faith in God, since we have never been able to move mountains. Such should be answered that we do not possess records of everything that hath come to pass in the Church, any more than, the Scripture being witness, we possess records of all the doings of our Lord Christ Himself. ~(John xx. 30; xxi. 25.) Mountains may have been removed and cast into the sea, in case of need; a like case, indeed, as we read, was that which came to pass at the prayers of the Blessed Father Gregory, Archbishop of Neo-Caesarea, in Pontus, that right worthy and mighty man, when a mountain was moved from one place on land to another place on land, as the dwellers in the city had need.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>E</c>cce enim Redemptóris voce decem vírgines, et omnes dicúntur vírgines, et tamen intra beatitúdinis jánuam non omnes sunt recéptæ; sunt quia eárum quædam, dum de virginitáte sua glóriam foris éxpetunt, in vasis suis óleum habére noluérunt. Sed sciéndum nobis est quod sæpe in sacro elóquio regnum cælórum præséntis témporis Ecclésia dícitur. quæ quia ex utróque sexu fidélium multitúdo collígitur, sancta Ecclésia decem virgínibus símilis esse denuntiátur. In qua quia mali cum bonis et réprobi cum eléctis commísti sunt, recte símilis virgínibus prudéntibus et fátuis esse perhibétur.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Eccli. 51</r>
<c>C</c>onfitébor tibi, Dómine Rex, et collaudábo te Deum salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>esu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:

<h>Q</h>ui pascis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.

<h>Q</h>uocúmque pergis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;

<h>T</h>e deprecámur lárgius,
Nostris adáuge sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória
Deo Patri et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur regi vírgines post eam.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
b61eb9430b:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Eccli. 51</r>
<c>I</c> will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.

<h>A</h>mongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.

<h>T</h>hey, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.

<h>W</h>e pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<h>Lesson 4</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May God the Father almighty be gracious and merciful unto us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
From the Sermons of St Maximus, Bishop [of Turin.] It is idle to strive to add anything to the praise of our holy and most blessed Father Gregorius whose Feast is this day kept. The beauty of his life ought not to be the subject of panegyrics, so much as the object of imitation. The Scripture saith “A wise son is the glory of his father,” truly then will he be honoured by such as, by doing after his en sample, show themselves to be his children for in Christ Jesus hath he begotten us through the Gospel.(1 Cor. iv. 15.)
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>U</c>nde et illi qui suórum adultéria et probra venerántur, cælibátus et viduitátis statuére pœnas; ut, ǽmuli críminum, mulctárent stúdia virtútum, spécie quidem qua fœcunditátem quǽrerent, sed stúdio quo propósitum castitátis abolérent. Vírginis Nec conféctis et miles stipéndiis arma depónit, et relícto offício quod gerébat, ad própria veteránus rura dimíttitur; ut et ipse exércitæ labóribus vitæ réquiem consequátur et álios spes futúræ quiétis subeúndis fáciat opéribus promptióres. Agrícola quoque matúrior torquéndam áliis stivam commíttit, et juveníli gravátus ópere, providéntiam curæ senílis explórat: vitem facílius tondére quam prémere, ut juvenescéntem luxúriam réprimat, et adolescéntem lascíviam falce succídat; parcórum quamdam pártuum castitátem docens étiam in vítibus expeténdam.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Lesson 5</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the mercy of Christ bring us to the joys of paradise.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
Therefore they who worship adultery and uncleanness in their gods made celibacy and widowhood punishable. They who lusted after abominations, taxed self-control. The pretence was the desire of fruitfulness, but the aim was to abolish virginity, the resolution of chastity. When a soldier hath served his time he layeth down his arms, leaveth his trade, and retireth him to his own lands, that as well himself may rest after the toils of life, as that the hope of rest to come may make others the more ready to undergo work. So also the aged labourer leaveth it for others to guide the handle of the plough, and withdraweth from the weariness of his younger days' labour to essay the task of an old man's thoughtful supervision. It is easier to prune vines, than to stamp them out, to check the first wild outburst of their vigour, and to curtail the wantonness of their young growth, so teaching, even by the example of the vineyard, that chastity, which keepeth itself within the bearing of but a few children.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cujus celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit ejus
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cujus túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis ejus méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

His hands are turned and as of gold, full of hyacinths. His belly as of ivory, set with sapphires. His legs as pillars of marble, that are set upon bases of gold. I to my beloved, and my beloved to me, who feedeth among the lilies. Thou art beautiful, O my love, sweet and comely as Jerusalem: terrible as an army set in array. Turn away thy eyes from me, for they have made me flee away. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from Galaad. Thy teeth as a flock of sheep, which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them. Thy cheeks are as the bark of a pomegranate, beside what is hidden within thee. <c>A</c>ve maris stella,

<r>Hymn</r>
<n>The first verse of the following hymn is said genuflecting.</n>
<c>A</c>ve, star of ocean,
Child divine who barest,
Mother, ever-Virgin,
Heaven's portal fairest.

<h>T</h>aking that sweet Ave
Erst by Gabriel spoken,
Eva's name reversing,
Be of peace the token.

<h>B</h>reak the sinners' fetters,
Light to blind restoring,
All our ills dispelling,
Every boon imploring.

<h>S</h>how thyself a mother
In thy supplication;
He will hear who chose thee
At his incarnation.

<h>M</h>aid all maids excelling,
Passing meek and lowly,
Win for sinners pardon,
Make us chaste and holy.

<h>A</h>s we onward journey
Aid our weak endeavour,
Till we gaze on Jesus
And rejoice forever.

<h>F</h>ather, Son, and Spirit,
Three in One confessing,
Give we equal glory
Equal praise and blessing.
Amen.

<c>S</c>ed, si caro Verbi Dei secúndum carnem nascéntis a carne Vírginis matris pronuntiátur extránea, sine causa venter qui eam portásset, úbera quæ lactássent, beatificántur. Dicit enim Apóstolus: Quia misit Deus Fílium suum, factum ex mulíere, factum sub lege. Neque audiéndi sunt, qui legéndum putant: Natum ex mulíere, factum sub lege, sed Factum ex mulíere; quia concéptus ex útero virgináli, carnem non de níhilo, non aliúnde, sed matérna traxit ex carne. Alióquin nec vere Fílius hóminis dicerétur, qui oríginem non habéret ex hómine.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>A</c>ve maris stella,
Dei Mater alma,
Atque semper Virgo,
Felix cæli porta.

<h>S</h>umens illud Ave
Gabriélis ore,
Funda nos in pace,
Mutans Hevæ nomen.

<h>S</h>olve vincla reis,
Profer lumen cæcis,
Mala nostra pelle,
Bona cuncta posce.

<h>M</h>onstra te esse matrem,
Sumat per te preces,
Qui pro nobis natus,
Tulit esse tuus.

<h>V</h>irgo singuláris,
Inter omnes mitis,
Nos culpis solútos
Mites fac et castos.

<h>V</h>itam præsta puram,
Iter para tutum,
Ut vidéntes Jesum,
Semper collætémur.

<h>S</h>it laus Deo Patri,
Summo Christo decus,
Spirítui Sancto,
Tribus honor unus.
Amen.

<r>Hymn</r>
<n>The first verse of the following hymn is said genuflecting.</n>
<c>A</c>ve, star of ocean,
Child divine who barest,
Mother, ever-Virgin,
Heaven's portal fairest.

<h>T</h>aking that sweet Ave
Erst by Gabriel spoken,
Eva's name reversing,
Be of peace the token.

<h>B</h>reak the sinners' fetters,
Light to blind restoring,
All our ills dispelling,
Every boon imploring.

<h>S</h>how thyself a mother
In thy supplication;
He will hear who chose thee
At his incarnation.

<h>M</h>aid all maids excelling,
Passing meek and lowly,
Win for sinners pardon,
Make us chaste and holy.

<h>A</h>s we onward journey
Aid our weak endeavour,
Till we gaze on Jesus
And rejoice forever.

<h>F</h>ather, Son, and Spirit,
Three in One confessing,
Give we equal glory
Equal praise and blessing.
Amen.

<c>S</c>on of a virgin, maker of thy mother,

Hear our petition!

Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.

Heavenly guerdon.

<c>C</c>onfitébor tibi Dómine rex, et collaudábo te Deum salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne, a láqueo linguæ iníquæ, et a lábiis operántium mendácium, et in conspéctu astántium factus es mihi adjútor.  Et liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de portis tribulatiónum quæ circumdedérunt me: a pressúra flammæ, quæ circúmdedit me, et in médio ignis non sum æstuátus: de altitúdine ventris ínferi, et a lingua coinquináta, et a verbo mendácii, a rege iníquo, et a lingua injústa:

<r>Ecclesiasticus 51:1-7</r>
A prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach. I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me. And hast preserved my body from destruction, from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of them that forge lies, and in the sight of them that stood by, thou hast been my helper. And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour. Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about: From the oppression of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burnt. From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, from an unjust king, and from a slanderous tongue:
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.

<h>H</h>e recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.

<h>B</h>ravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.

<h>W</h>ith humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.

<h>G</h>lory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

<c>I</c>n illo témpore : Dixit Jesus turbis: Si quis venit ad me, et non odit patrem suum, et matrem, et uxórem, et fílios, et fratres, et soróres, adhuc autem et ánimam suam, non potest meus esse discípulus. Et réliqua.
<r>Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ. (Hom. 37. in Evang.)</r>
<c>S</c>i considerémus fratres caríssimi, quæ et quanta sunt, quæ nobis promittúntur in cælis, viléscunt ánimo ómnia quæ habéntur in terris. Terréna namque substántia supérnæ felicitáti comparáta, pondus est, non subsídium. Temporális vita ætérnæ vitæ comparáta, mors est pótius dicénda quam vita, Ipse enim quotidianus deféctus corruptiónis quid est áliud, quam quædam prolíxitas mortis? Quæ autem lingua dícere, vel quis intelléctus cápere súfficit, illa supérnæ civitátis quanta sint gáudia; Angelórum choris interésse, cum beatíssimis spirítibus glóriæ Conditóris assístere, præséntem Dei vultum cérnere, incircumscríptum lumen vidére, nullo mortis metu áffici, incorruptiónis perpétuæ múnere lætári?
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>S</c>ed ad hæc audíta inardéscit ánimus, jamque illic cupit assístere, ubi sc sperat sine fine gaudére. Sed ad magna prǽmia perveníri non potest, nisi per magnos labóres. Unde et Paulus egrégius prædicátor dicit: Non coronábitur, nisi qui legítime certáverit. Deléctet ergo mentem magnitúdo præmiórum, sed non detérreat certámen labórum. Unde ad se veniéntibus Véritas dicit: Si quis venit ad me, et non odit patrem suum, et matrem, et uxórem, et fílios, et fratres, et soróres, adhuc autem et ánimam suam, non potest meus esse discípulus.

Then we hear these things our hearts burn within us and we long to be already there, where we hope to rejoice for ever. But we cannot attain unto great rewards, save through great labour. Therefore saith the excellent preacher Paul: “He is not crowned, except he strive lawfully.” (2 Tim. ii. 5.) The greatness of the reward doth delight our mind let not the throes of the struggle dishearten us. Therefore the Truth saith unto every one that cometh unto Him “If any man come to Me, and hate not his father and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be My disciple.”

<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
